correctness.rationale: For a,b>=3, distance exactly two holds precisely between distinct same-shore vertices; defence constraints factor shorewise. The displayed F_s and H_s polynomials count all shore labelings and a specified positive vertex. Any isolated positive in the support graph must face a singleton opposite support at a deleted matching edge. Each edge gives two classes of failures, intersection exactly one weight-four labeling, and distinct deleted-edge failure families are disjoint. Inclusion-exclusion proves the full polynomial. Evaluation and degree bounds follow directly. Direct independent BFS and original-definition exhaustive checks passed for 28 parameter triples (523422 labelings).

value.rationale: The result is a complete weight distribution on a natural infinite class of dense bipartite graphs, together with a structural affine response under t simultaneous edge deletions; its failure-event mechanism explains why interactions do not appear when deleted edges are disjoint. This is mathematically richer than an already-known minimum of four: each coefficient, total count, minimum count and a high-weight stability cutoff are determined, with plausible use in enumerative and extremal comparisons of hop-total-Roman configurations.
